To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microstructure and solidification of gas-atomised Al-Fe-(VI) alloy powders are controlled by the competition between growth of a-Al phase fronts and freely-nucleated icosahedrally-dense phase (I) particles.
the microstructural morphology and solidification behavior of gas-atomized Al-Fe-(v, Si) alloy powder is influenced by the alloy chemistry, powder size and solidification rate.
The solidification behavior of Al-Fe-V alloy powder particles was attributed to a competition of α−aluminum growth and freely nucleated quasicrystallites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of Al-based alloys with improved wear properties.
the development of AlFe-V-Si alloys with high specific strength, good ductility and high wear resistance.
the solidification behavior of Al-Fe-V and Al-Fe-V−Si alloy powders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the solidification of Al-75Fe-5V and Al-75Fe-V-5Si alloy powders would proceed by a cellular-dendritic mechanism, and a micro-quasicrystal phase would form by nucleation and growth in intercellular and interdendritic regions.

the solidification of Al- Fe-(V, Si ) alloy powders is a complex phenomenon involving a number of factors including the composition and the solidification rate, the presence of dispersed particles, and the interaction between solidification fronts and the dispersed particles.

the solidification behavior of Al-Fe-V and Al-Fe-V−Si alloys is a complex phenomenon, and the microstructures of the alloy powders would strongly depend on alloy compositions, solidification conditions, and cooling rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the solidification behavior of Al-Fe-V alloy powder would be controlled by solidification rate and the microstructural morphology would be determined by the competition between the growth of the α−aluminium solidification fronts and the freely nucleated icoahedral particles.

the microstructures of Al-Fe-V alloy powder are dominated by the competition between the growth of α−Al phase fronts and freely-nucleated icosahedrons, and that the microstructures are influenced by solidification rate.

the microstructures of the Al-15wt%Fe-2wt%V alloy powder were controlled by solidification rate and powder size, and the microstructures of Al-15wt.%Fe-2wt.%V-3wt%Si alloy powder were controlled mainly by solidification rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microstructural morphology of Al-Fe alloy powders can be tailored by adjusting alloying composition and/or processing conditions.
solidification of the Al- Fe-(V, Si ) alloy powders can be controlled by the solidification conditions, which would lead to the formation of a variety of microstructures.
the solidification behavior of AlFe-(V, S) alloy powders can be controlled by adjusting the alloy composition and solidification rates.
